fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. The LORD gives Moses His reason: “…because I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.” Ar was already given to someone else. So the instruction to Israel is to leave the Moabites alone, and driving them out is the opposite of that.

Twelve is a long stretch already, friend. But Moses gives a bigger number for the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered. He says it was “thirty-eight years.” That's more than three times twelve.

Seven years would be a long trip, I'll give you that. Moses puts the number much higher, though: “thirty-eight years.” That's how long the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered took. Seven doesn't even get you halfway.

Seir it is. Moses says, “…for many days we wandered around Mount Seir.” Many days around one mountain. You know when you circle the same block three times hunting for a parking spot? That's the kind of lap I'm picturing.

Carmel never shows up in this passage. Moses says that for many days they wandered around Mount Seir. It's like texting the wrong Mike when you've got three Mikes in your contacts. The name feels right, but it's the wrong one. Seir is the one.

Not this time, friend. The LORD tells Moses what to say to the people: “They will be afraid of you, so you must be very careful.” The ones He says will be afraid are the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. And Israel gets the instruction to be very careful.

That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, “…because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.” So He tells Israel there won't be any of that land for them, “not even a footprint.” Not even a footprint! I'd be checking my shoes at the border.

The text doesn't say anything about Israel asking or not asking. The LORD's reason is simple: “…because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.” His reason is about what He gave, not about a request.

Right on the money, and I mean that literally. The LORD says, “You are to pay them in silver for the food you eat and the water you drink.” That's His instruction for passing through Seir. I like it, friend. It's a clean way to treat a neighbor.
Free would be nice, I won't lie. I'd take free every time. But the LORD's instruction is to pay in silver. His words are, “You are to pay them in silver for the food you eat and the water you drink.”

Yes. The note says Esau's people drove out the Horites and settled in their place, “just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.” So the note holds up Israel's own settling in its land as the comparison. And it sits right in the middle of a travel report.
Not this time, friend. The LORD says, “Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered.” Then Moses says, “So we crossed over the Brook of Zered.” The command comes and the crossing follows.

True. When they get close to the Ammonites, the LORD says, “…do not harass them or provoke them…” His reason: “…for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites.” Another neighbor, and the same kind of instruction.
